s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging abdominal mass with intermittent high-grade fever and abdominal pain
salient_findings: Central abdominal lump
Intermittent high-grade fever
Dull, aching abdominal pain
Moderately tender mass in the umbilical region
Non-tender thickening of the right spermatic cord
Large, well-defined, unilocular cyst on abdominal ultrasonography
key_facts: 35-year-old man from rural north India
One-month history of progressively enlarging abdominal lump
Developed intermittent high-grade fever and abdominal pain three weeks after lump appeared
No significant past medical history
Moderately tender mass in the umbilical region on examination
Non-tender thickening of the right spermatic cord
Inguinal nodes were barely palpable
No lower-extremity edema
Normal complete blood counts and blood chemistry
Sterile blood cultures
Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a large, well-defined, unilocular cyst
Contrast-enhanced CT scan confirmed ultrasonography findings
Surgical exploration revealed a large retroperitoneal cyst
Cyst was completely excised with a well-defined avascular plane

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lymphangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a large, well-defined, unilocular cyst with a conglomeration of grossly dilated lymphatics near its upper pole

shortlist.label: Mesenteric cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the location and characteristics of the cyst, although less specific than retroperitoneal lymphangioma

shortlist.label: Mullerian duct cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the retroperitoneal location, but less likely due to the absence of specific features

shortlist.label: Lymphatic malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the lymphatic involvement, but retroperitoneal lymphangioma is a more specific diagnosis

shortlist.label: Enteric duplication cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Possible, although less likely due to the lack of specific features and the location of the cyst

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, well-defined, unilocular cyst in the retroperitoneal space with a conglomeration of grossly dilated lymphatics near its upper pole, as revealed by surgical exploration, strongly supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Mesenteric cyst
rejected.why: Although mesenteric cysts can present similarly, the specific location and lymphatic involvement point more towards a lymphangioma.

rejected.label: Mullerian duct cyst
rejected.why: Mullerian duct cysts are typically midline and not associated with lymphatic malformations.

rejected.label: Lymphatic malformation
rejected.why: While lymphatic malformation is a broader term that could encompass this condition, retroperitoneal lymphangioma is a more specific diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the cyst.

rejected.label: Enteric duplication cyst
rejected.why: Enteric duplication cysts are usually connected to the intestinal tract, which was not indicated in the surgical findings.
